questions.problem:
Using the change of variables $u=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}$ and $v=xy,$ evaluate the double integral

$$
{∬}_{D}xy\,dx\,dy,
$$

where $D={(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 4{x}^{2},\,1\le xy\le 5}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dx\,dy={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v),y(u,v))|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|du\,dv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}},\,v=xy
$$

 
gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows::

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uv$-plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & ={(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le 4,\,1\le v\le 5}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-\frac{2y}{{x}^{3}} & \frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\ y & \text{ }\text{ }x\end{aligned}| \\  & =-\frac{3y}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{(-\frac{3y}{{x}^{2}})}=-\frac{1}{3u}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}xy\,dx\,dy & ={∬}_{Δ}v|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}v\cdot |\frac{1}{3u}|\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{v}{u}\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{5}v[{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u]\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{5}v[\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|\,{|}_{1}^{4}]dv \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{5}v(\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)\,dv \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{3}{\int }_{1}^{5}v\,dv \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}\,{|}_{1}^{5} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{3}\cdot (25-1) \\  & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
u=x\,\text{and}\,v=x+y.
$$

$$

$$

$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & \text{ }\text{ }0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 1**: Find a suitable change of variables.

The integrand

$$
f(x,y)=(2x-y){e}^{(2x-y)^{2}}
$$

suggests that we use the change of variables 

$$
u=x,\,v=2x-y.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{aligned}].
$$

**Step 2**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

The vertices of our domain $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}(2,3) & =(2,2(2)-3) \\  & =(2,1) \\ {T}^{-1}(4,7) & =(4,2(4)-7) \\  & =(4,1) \\ {T}^{-1}(4,6) & =(4,2(4)-6) \\  & =(4,2) \\ {T}^{-1}(2,2) & =(2,2(2)-2) \\  & =(2,2)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our domain in the $uv$-plane is the following rectangle:

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,2\le u\le 4,\,1\le v\le 2}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096119/assets/e11ecccc49394915edd90a58c77ac96e08f22eb5a41d7e7eb6bdbb5af2890c94.png)

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=-1
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 5**: Perform the change of variables, and evaluate the integral:

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}(2x-y){e}^{(2x-y)^{2}}\,\text{d}x\text{d}y & ={∬}_{Δ}v{e}^{{v}^{2}}\,|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}v{e}^{{v}^{2}}\,|-1|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2}^{4}v{e}^{{v}^{2}}\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}v{e}^{{v}^{2}}\,\text{d}v{\int }_{2}^{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}{e}^{{v}^{2}}]}_{1}^{2}\cdot {[u]}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{4}-e)\cdot 2 \\  & ={e}^{4}-e.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dxdy={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v),y(u,v))\,|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows:

**Step 1**: Find a suitable change of variables.

The integrand

$$
f(x,y)=(\frac{x}{2}+y){e}^{x+3y}
$$

suggests that we use the change of variables 

$$
u=\frac{x}{2}+y\,v=x+3y.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{aligned}].
$$

**Step 2**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

The vertices of our domain $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}(8,-3) & =(\frac{8}{2}+(-3),8+3(-3)) \\  & =(1,-1) \\ {T}^{-1}(10,-4) & =(\frac{10}{2}+(-4),10+3(-4)) \\  & =(1,-2) \\ {T}^{-1}(16,-6) & =(\frac{16}{2}+(-6),16+3(-6)) \\  & =(2,-2) \\ {T}^{-1}(14,-5) & =(\frac{14}{2}+(-5),14+3(-5)) \\  & =(2,-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our domain in the $uv$-plane is the following rectangle:

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le 2,\,-2\le v\le -1}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096119/assets/2190993a44d34264ced80e163c81a49bd13fa4cfb4c70814655284564bcbb2cf.png)

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=2
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 5**: Perform the change of variables, and evaluate the integral:

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}(\frac{x}{2}+y){e}^{x+3y}\,\text{d}x\text{d}y & ={∬}_{Δ}u{e}^{v}\,|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}u{e}^{v}\,|2|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{-2}^{-1}{\int }_{1}^{2}u{e}^{v}\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{-2}^{-1}{e}^{v}\,\text{d}v{\int }_{1}^{2}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\cdot [{e}^{v}]_{-2}^{-1}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}v \\  & =2\cdot (\frac{1}{e}-\frac{1}{{e}^{2}})\cdot \frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{3(e-1)}{{e}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the region $D$ in the $xy$-plane, given by

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: -2 \leq 4x+2y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq y-x \leq 3 \big\}.
$$

By performing the change of variables $u = 4x+2y$ and $v=y - x,$ write the following integral in terms of $u$ and $v.$ 

$$
\displaystyle 
\iint\limits_D \sin \left(3(x+y)\right)  \: \mathrm{d}x \, \mathrm{d}y
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $\mathbf{T}$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096119/assets/b83369a26291155dbb8a5031d91fcf869cff259b7c170b6a15d58d317cee934d.png)

This transformation maps some region $\Delta$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
\iint\limits_{D} f(x,y) \, \mathrm d x \, \mathrm d y = \iint\limits_{\Delta} \ f(x(u,v), y(u,v))  \left| \dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)} \right|  \mathrm d u \, \mathrm d v
$$

where $\dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf{T}.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u = 4x + 2y, \qquad v = y - x
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function $\mathbf T^{-1},$ that is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096119/assets/461f793c9e8d6c3e5e5f67f846bade4acea9d40dc6c3975659d60167c33f6579.png)

To compute the required integral, we proceed as follows:

**Step 1**: Find $\Delta,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uv$-plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & ={(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 3}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T^{-1}.$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -1 & \text{ }\text{ }1\end{aligned}| \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T.$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T$ is

$$
\dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)} = \left( \dfrac{\partial (u, v)}{\partial (x, y)} \right)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{6}.
$$

Note that $\dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)} \neq 0$ everywhere inside $\Delta.$ In other words, $\mathbf T$ has no critical points inside $\Delta.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables.

In this case, we first need to solve the transformation equations

$$
u = 4x+2y, \qquad v = y-x
$$

 
for $x$ and $y$, which gives

$$
x = \dfrac{u-2v}6, \qquad y =\dfrac{u+4v}6.
$$

 

Performing the change of variables, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(x+y))\,dx\,dy & ={∬}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(\frac{u-2v}{6}+\frac{u+4v}{6}))|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(\frac{2u+2v}{6}))|\frac{1}{6}|\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{2}sin\,(u+v)\,du\,dv.\end{aligned}
$$
